title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 24: Three Sons of Emperor Yang

sentences.zh: 元德太子元德太子昭，煬帝長子也，生而高祖命養宮中。

translations.literal: Yuande Crown Prince Zhao was Emperor Yang's eldest son; from birth the Emperor Gaozu ordered that he be raised in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuande Crown Prince, Zhao, was Emperor Yang's firstborn son. From infancy Emperor Wen had ordered him brought up within the palace.

sentences.zh: 三歲時，於玄武門弄石師子，高祖與文獻後至其所。

translations.literal: At age three, at the Xuanwu Gate he was playing with a stone lion; the Emperor Gaozu and Empress Wenxian came to where he was.
translations.idiomatic: When he was three, he was playing with a stone lion at the Xuanwu Gate. Emperor Wen and Empress Wenxian came to where he was.

sentences.zh: 高祖適患腰痛，舉手憑後，昭因避去，如此者再三。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu happened to be suffering from lower-back pain and raised his hand to lean on the empress; Zhao thereupon drew back, and this happened several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen happened to be troubled by lower-back pain and raised his hand to lean on the empress. Zhao each time drew back, and this happened again and again.

sentences.zh: 高祖歎曰：「天生長者，誰複教乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu sighed and said: "Born a man of propriety—who could still need to teach him!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sighed and said, "Born a man of propriety—who could still need to teach him!"

sentences.zh: 」由是大奇之。

translations.literal: Because of this he considered the boy extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: From this he regarded the boy as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗謂曰：「當為爾娶婦。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu once said to him: "I shall find you a wife."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told him, "I shall find you a wife."

sentences.zh: 」昭應聲而泣。

translations.literal: Zhao answered with a burst of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao burst into tears at once.

sentences.zh: 高祖問其故，對曰：「漢王未婚時，恆在至尊所，一朝娶婦，便則出外。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu asked the reason; he replied: "Before the Prince of Han was married, he always stayed at Your Majesty's side; once he took a wife, he at once went out of the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen asked why. He replied, "Before the Prince of Han married, he always stayed at Your Majesty's side. Once he took a wife, he at once left the palace."

sentences.zh: 懼將違離，是以啼耳。

translations.literal: "I fear I am about to be parted from you, and therefore I weep."
translations.idiomatic: "I fear I am about to be separated from you—that is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 」上歎其有至性，特鍾愛焉。

translations.literal: The sovereign marveled at his innate devotion and lavished special affection on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at his innate devotion and lavished special affection on him.

sentences.zh: 年十二，立為河南王。

translations.literal: At twelve he was enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，徙為晉王，拜內史令，兼左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was transferred to Prince of Jin, appointed Inner Secretariat Director, and concurrently Grand General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was made Prince of Jin, appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat, and concurrently Grand General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 後三年，轉雍州牧。

translations.literal: Three years later he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，便幸洛陽宮，昭留守京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he at once went to the Luoyang palace; Zhao remained to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he at once went to the Luoyang palace while Zhao remained to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: ，帝遣使者立為皇太子。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to invest him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to invest him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 昭有武力，能引強弩。

translations.literal: Zhao had physical strength and could draw heavy crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was physically strong and could draw heavy crossbows.

sentences.zh: 性謙沖，言色恂恂，未嘗忿怒。

translations.literal: His nature was modest and restrained; in speech and bearing he was uniformly gentle and he never showed anger.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was modest and restrained; in speech and bearing he was uniformly gentle, and he never showed anger.

sentences.zh: 有深嫌可責者，但雲「大不是」。

translations.literal: When someone had done something that deeply warranted reproach, he would only say, "That is quite wrong."
translations.idiomatic: When someone had done something that deeply warranted reproach, he would only say, "That is quite wrong."

sentences.zh: 所膳不許多品，帷席極於儉素。

translations.literal: His meals never comprised many dishes; curtains and mats were exceedingly plain.
translations.idiomatic: His meals never comprised many dishes; curtains and mats were exceedingly plain.

sentences.zh: 臣吏有老父母者，必親問其安否，歲時皆有惠賜。

translations.literal: If an official had aged parents, he would personally inquire after their well-being; at the seasons he always had gifts bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: If an official had aged parents, he would personally inquire after their well-being, and at each season he always had gifts bestowed.

sentences.zh: 其仁愛如此。

translations.literal: Such was his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 明年，朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: In the following year he attended court at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attended court at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後數月，將還京師，願得少留，帝不許，拜請無數。

translations.literal: Several months later, as he was about to return to the capital, he wished to remain a little longer; the emperor did not permit it, and despite countless pleas…
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, as he was about to return to the capital, he wished to remain a little longer. The emperor would not permit it, and despite countless pleas…

sentences.zh: 體素肥，因致勞疾。

translations.literal: His constitution had always been corpulent, and he fell ill from exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: His constitution had always been heavyset, and he fell ill from exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 帝令巫者視之，雲：「房陵王為祟。

translations.literal: The emperor had a shaman examine him; the man said: "Prince of Fangling is the malign influence."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a shaman examine him. The man said, "Prince of Fangling is the malign influence."

sentences.zh: 」未幾而薨。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 詔內史侍郎虞世基為哀冊文曰：

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yu Shiji to compose an elegiac scroll, which reads:
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Secretariat Vice Minister Yu Shiji to compose an elegiac scroll, which reads:

sentences.zh: :維七月癸丑朔二十三日，皇太子薨于行宮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day, the cyclical day guichou of the seventh month, the crown prince died at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day—the cyclical day guichou of the seventh month—the crown prince died at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 粵三年五月庚辰朔六日，將遷座于莊陵，禮也。

translations.literal: On the sixth day, the cyclical day gengchen, of the fifth month in the third year, the coffin shall be transferred to Zhuang Mausoleum—such is the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day—the cyclical day gengchen of the fifth month in the third year—the coffin shall be transferred to Zhuang Mausoleum. Such is the ritual.

sentences.zh: 蜃綍宵載，鶴關曉辟，肅文物以具陳，儼賓從其如昔。

translations.literal: The imperial catafalque is borne forth by night; at dawn the Spirit Gate opens; solemnly the regalia is marshaled, and the escort stands as of old.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial catafalque moves by night; at dawn the Spirit Gate opens. The ritual regalia is fully arrayed, and the escort stands as in former times.

sentences.zh: 皇帝悼離方之雲晦，嗟震宮之虧象，顧守器以長懷，臨登餕而興想。

translations.literal: The emperor grieves that clouds darken the distant quarter and laments the image broken in the Eastern Palace; he looks upon the vessel of state with long sorrow and, facing the ascent to the funeral feast, is moved to thought.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieves that clouds darken the distant quarter and laments the image shattered in the Eastern Palace. He looks upon the vessel of state with enduring sorrow and, facing the ascent to the funeral feast, is stirred to thought.

sentences.zh: 先遠戒日，占謀允從，庭彝徹祖，階所收重，抗銘旌以啟路，動徐輪于振容。

translations.literal: The day of distant warning is appointed and the divination agrees; the court ritual vessels are removed from the ancestral hall and the steps receive the bier; the inscribed banner is raised to open the way, and the slow wheels move within the mourning screen.
translations.idiomatic: The day of distant warning is appointed and the divination agrees. The court ritual vessels are removed from the ancestral hall and the steps receive the bier. The inscribed banner is raised to open the way, and the slow wheels move within the mourning screen.

sentences.zh: 揆行度名，累德彰諡，爰詔史冊，式遵典志，俾浚哲之徽猷，播長久乎天地。

translations.literal: Surveying conduct to fix the name, accumulating virtue to manifest the posthumous title—thus he decrees the historical record, following the canonical pattern, so that the lofty wisdom may spread long through heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying conduct to fix the name and accumulating virtue to manifest the posthumous title—thus he decrees the historical record, following the canonical pattern, so that lofty wisdom may spread long through heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: :宸基峻極，帝緒會昌。

translations.literal: The imperial foundation towers to the utmost; the imperial succession gathers prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial foundation towers to the utmost; the imperial succession gathers prosperity.

sentences.zh: 體元襲聖，儀耀重光。

translations.literal: Embodying the origin and inheriting sagehood, his splendor redoubles the radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Embodying the origin and inheriting sagehood, his splendor redoubles the radiance.

sentences.zh: 氣秀春陸，神華少陽。

translations.literal: His vitality flourished like spring on the earth; his spirit blossomed in the young yang.
translations.idiomatic: His vitality flourished like spring upon the earth; his spirit blossomed in the young yang.

sentences.zh: 居周軼誦，處漢韜莊。

translations.literal: In Zhou he exceeded the recitations; in Han he concealed his plenitude.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou he surpassed the recitations; in Han he concealed his fullness.

sentences.zh: 有縱生知，誕膺惟睿。

translations.literal: He had from birth knowledge beyond measure and received the sole sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed knowledge from birth beyond measure and received the sole sagacity.

sentences.zh: 性道觿日，幾深綺歲。

translations.literal: The Way and character showed in infancy; subtleties were grasped in splendid youth.
translations.idiomatic: The Way and character showed in infancy; subtleties were grasped in splendid youth.

sentences.zh: 降跡大成，俯情多藝。

translations.literal: He descended to trace the great completion and bent his sentiments to many arts.
translations.idiomatic: He descended to trace the great completion and bent his sentiments to many arts.

sentences.zh: 樹親建國，命懿作籓。

translations.literal: He planted kinship and established states; fate and virtue made him a border prince.
translations.idiomatic: He planted kinship and established states; fate and virtue made him a border prince.

sentences.zh: 威蕤先路，舄奕渠門。

translations.literal: Majestic array took the lead; glittering train filled the gate-towers.
translations.idiomatic: Majestic array took the lead; a glittering train filled the gate-towers.

sentences.zh: 庸服有紀，分器惟尊。

translations.literal: Service had its statutes; shares in ritual vessels held honor alone.
translations.idiomatic: Service had its statutes; shares in ritual vessels held honor alone.

sentences.zh: 風高楚殿，雅盛梁園。

translations.literal: The wind rose high in the Chu hall; elegance flourished in the Liang garden.
translations.idiomatic: The wind rose high in the Chu hall; elegance flourished in the Liang garden.

sentences.zh: 睿後膺儲，天人協順。

translations.literal: The sagely heir received investiture; heaven and man joined in accord.
translations.idiomatic: The sagely heir received investiture; heaven and man joined in accord.

sentences.zh: 本茂條遠，基崇體峻。

translations.literal: The root was thick and the branches far; the base was high and the body lofty.
translations.idiomatic: The root was thick and the branches far; the base was high and the body lofty.

sentences.zh: 改王參墟，奄有唐、晉。

translations.literal: He was transferred from Prince of Wei to the lands of Tang and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from Prince of Wei to the lands of Tang and Jin.

sentences.zh: 在貴能謙，居沖益慎。

translations.literal: In exalted station he could be humble; in the central position he grew more cautious.
translations.idiomatic: In exalted station he could be humble; in the central position he grew more cautious.

sentences.zh: 封畿千里，閶闔九重。

translations.literal: A thousand li of the domain; ninefold gates of the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li of the domain; ninefold gates of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 神州王化，禁旅軍容。

translations.literal: The Central Land knew royal transformation; the forbidden guard bore military array.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Land knew royal transformation; the forbidden guard bore military array.

sentences.zh: 瞻言偃草，高視折衝。

translations.literal: A glance made weeds lie down; a high gaze broke the foe.
translations.idiomatic: A glance made weeds lie down; a high gaze broke the foe.

sentences.zh: 帷扆清秘，親賢允屬。

translations.literal: Within the curtain, the secrets were clear; kin and worthies were rightly placed.
translations.idiomatic: Within the curtain the secrets were clear; kin and worthies were rightly placed.

sentences.zh: 泛景風瀾，飛華螭玉。

translations.literal: He sailed the glowing tide of breeze; flew the splendor of horn and jade.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed the glowing tide of breeze and flew the splendor of horn and jade.

sentences.zh: 揮翰泉湧，敷言藻縟。

translations.literal: His brush poured like a spring; his spread words were brocade.
translations.idiomatic: His brush poured like a spring; his spread words were brocade.

sentences.zh: 式是便煩，思謀啟沃。

translations.literal: Thus he shared the burdensome affairs and planned to open the aiding flow.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he shared burdensome affairs and planned to open the aiding flow.

sentences.zh: 洪惟積德，豐衍繁祉。

translations.literal: Greatly was accumulated virtue; abundant blessings multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly was virtue accumulated; abundant blessings multiplied.

sentences.zh: 粵自天孫，光升元子。

translations.literal: From the Heaven Grandson came the light that ascended the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: From the Heaven Grandson came the light that ascended the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 綠車逮事，翠纓奉祀。

translations.literal: The green carriage attended affairs; the kingfisher tassel led the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The green carriage attended affairs; the kingfisher tassel led the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 肅穆滿容，儀形讓齒。

translations.literal: Solemn reverence filled his bearing; demeanor and form yielded precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn reverence filled his bearing; demeanor and form yielded precedence.

sentences.zh: 禮樂交暢，愛敬兼資。

translations.literal: Ritual and music exchanged freely; love and respect were both present.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music exchanged freely; love and respect were both present.

sentences.zh: 優遊養德，恭己承儀。

translations.literal: He roamed at ease to nurture virtue; respectful in himself, he bore the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He roamed at ease to nurture virtue; respectful in himself, he bore the rites.

sentences.zh: 南山聘隱，東序尊師。

translations.literal: In the southern hills he sought hermits; in the eastern school he honored teachers.
translations.idiomatic: In the southern hills he sought hermits; in the eastern school he honored teachers.

sentences.zh: 有粹神儀，深穆其度。

translations.literal: He had pure spirit and bearing; depth and solemnity in measure.
translations.idiomatic: He had pure spirit and bearing, depth and solemnity in measure.

sentences.zh: 顯顯觀德，溫溫審諭。

translations.literal: Brightly he displayed his virtue; warmly he examined instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly he displayed his virtue; warmly he examined instruction.

sentences.zh: 炯戒齊箴，留連王賦。

translations.literal: Vigilant admonition and highest caution; lingering over royal compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Vigilant admonition and highest caution; lingering over royal compositions.

sentences.zh: 入監出撫，日就月將。

translations.literal: Entering to supervise, going forth to comfort—day by day advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Entering to supervise and going forth to comfort—day by day advancing.

sentences.zh: 沖情玉裕，令問金相。

translations.literal: Serene sentiment, jade abundance; fine reputation, metal radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Serene sentiment, jade abundance; fine reputation, metal radiance.

sentences.zh: 宜綏景福，永作元良。

translations.literal: He should have soothed bright fortune and long served as the eldest heir.
translations.idiomatic: He should have soothed bright fortune and long served as the eldest heir.

sentences.zh: 神理冥漠，天道難究。

translations.literal: The divine principle is dark and silent; heaven's way is hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: The divine principle is dark and silent; heaven's way is hard to fathom.

sentences.zh: 仁不必壽，善或愆祐。

translations.literal: Benevolence does not assure long life; goodness may forfeit blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence does not assure long life; goodness may forfeit blessing.

sentences.zh: 遽瑤山之頹壞，忽桂宮之毀構。

translations.literal: Suddenly the jade mountain tottered; swiftly the cassia palace fell.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the jade mountain tottered; swiftly the cassia palace fell.

sentences.zh: 痛結幽明，悲纏宇宙。

translations.literal: Grief bound the hidden and the manifest; sorrow entwined the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Grief bound the hidden and the manifest; sorrow entwined the cosmos.

sentences.zh: 慟皇情之深憫，摧具僚其如疚。

translations.literal: The emperor's sorrow was deeply pitiful; all officials were crushed as by guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's sorrow was deeply pitiful; all officials were crushed as by guilt.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas, the grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas, the grief!

sentences.zh: 回環氣朔，荏苒居諸。

translations.literal: The qi and calendar turn in cycle; time flows on.
translations.idiomatic: The qi and calendar turn in cycle; time flows on.

sentences.zh: 沾零露於瑤圍，下申霜於玉除。

translations.literal: Zero dew falls on the jade enclosure; early frost descends on the jade steps.
translations.idiomatic: Zero dew falls on the jade enclosure; early frost descends on the jade steps.

sentences.zh: 夜漏盡兮空階曙，曉月懸兮帷殿虛。

translations.literal: Night water runs out—empty steps at dawn; the morning moon hangs—the curtained hall deserted.
translations.idiomatic: The night water runs out—empty steps at dawn; the morning moon hangs—the curtained hall deserted.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas, the grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas, the grief!

sentences.zh: 將寧甫竁，長違望苑。

translations.literal: He is about to rest in the southern tomb, long parting from the Park of Hope.
translations.idiomatic: He is about to rest in the southern tomb, long parting from the Park of Hope.

sentences.zh: 渡渭涘於造舟，遵長平之修阪。

translations.literal: Crossing the Wei ford by the ferry bridge, following the long slope of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Wei ford by the ferry bridge, following the long slope of Changping.

sentences.zh: 望鶴駕而不追，顧龍樓而日遠。

translations.literal: Gazing at the crane carriage yet unable to pursue; looking back at the dragon tower, daily farther away.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the crane carriage yet unable to pursue; looking back at the dragon tower, daily farther away.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas, the grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas, the grief!

sentences.zh: 永隔存沒，長分古今。

translations.literal: Forever parted in life and death; long divided between past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Forever parted in life and death; long divided between past and present.

sentences.zh: 去榮華于人世，即潛之幽深。

translations.literal: He leaves splendor in the human world and enters the depth of the hidden earth.
translations.idiomatic: He leaves splendor in the human world and enters the depth of the hidden earth.

sentences.zh: 霏夕煙而稍起，慘落景而將沉。

translations.literal: Evening mist rises thinly; the sinking sunset light is about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Evening mist rises thinly; the sinking sunset light is about to fall.

sentences.zh: 聽哀挽之悽楚，雜灌木之悲吟。

translations.literal: Hearing the mournful funeral dirge; mingled with the shrubs' sad chant.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the mournful funeral dirge mingled with the shrubs' sad chant.

sentences.zh: 紛徒禦而流袂，欷纓弁以沾衿。

translations.literal: The attendants brush sleeves with tears; hats and ribbons are wet upon the collar.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brush sleeves with tears; hats and ribbons are wet upon the collar.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas, the grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas, the grief!

sentences.zh: 九地黃泉，千年白日。

translations.literal: Ninefold earth, yellow spring; a thousand years, white sun.
translations.idiomatic: Ninefold earth, yellow spring; a thousand years, white sun.

sentences.zh: 雖金石之能久，終天壤乎長畢。

translations.literal: Though metal and stone endure long, in the end heaven and earth reach completion.
translations.idiomatic: Though metal and stone endure long, in the end heaven and earth reach completion.

sentences.zh: 敢圖芳於篆素，永飛聲而騰實。

translations.literal: I dare inscribe fragrance on bamboo and silk, forever letting his fame soar in reality.
translations.idiomatic: I dare inscribe fragrance on bamboo and silk, forever letting his fame soar in reality.

sentences.zh: 帝深追悼。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 有子三人，韋妃生恭皇帝，大劉良娣生燕王倓，小劉良娣生越王侗。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the Consort Wei bore Emperor Gong; the Senior Lady of Excellence Liu bore Prince of Yan Tan; the Junior Lady of Excellence Liu bore Prince of Yue Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Consort Wei bore Emperor Gong; the senior Lady of Excellence Liu bore Prince of Yan Tan; the junior Lady of Excellence Liu bore Prince of Yue Tong.

sentences.zh: 燕王燕王倓字仁安。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Tan, styled Ren'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan Tan, styled Ren'an.

sentences.zh: 敏慧美姿儀，煬帝于諸孫中特所鍾愛，常置左右。

translations.literal: Clever and handsome in bearing, among all grandsons Emperor Yang especially cherished him and often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and handsome in bearing, among all grandsons Emperor Yang especially cherished him and often kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 性好讀書，尤重儒素，非造次所及，有若成人。

translations.literal: His nature loved reading and especially valued Confucian plainness; what he achieved was not reached in haste and was like a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading and especially valued Confucian plainness. What he achieved was not reached in haste and was like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 良娣早終，每至忌日，末嘗不流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: The Lady of Excellence died early; on each anniversary he never failed to weep and sob.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Excellence died early; on each anniversary he never failed to weep and sob.

sentences.zh: 帝由是益以奇之。

translations.literal: The emperor for this reason prized him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor for this reason prized him all the more.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，倓覺變，欲入奏，恐露其事，因與梁公蕭钜、千牛宇文皛等穿芳林門側水竇而入。

translations.literal: At the time of Yu Wen Huaji's regicide, Tan perceived the upheaval and wished to enter to report it; fearing the matter would be exposed, he therefore with Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Palace Gentleman Yuwen Hao, and others passed through the water opening beside Fanglin Gate to enter.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Yu Wen Huaji's regicide, Tan perceived the upheaval and wished to enter and report it. Fearing the matter would be exposed, he passed through the water conduit beside Fanglin Gate with Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Palace Gentleman Yuwen Hao, and others to enter.

sentences.zh: 至玄武門，詭奏曰：「臣卒中惡，命縣俄頃，請得面辭，死無所恨。

translations.literal: Reaching the Xuanwu Gate, he made a false report, saying: "Your subject has been suddenly stricken with a malign affliction; my life hangs by a moment. I beg to be granted a face-to-face farewell—then death will hold no regret."
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuanwu Gate he made a false report: "Your subject has been suddenly stricken with a malign affliction; my life hangs by a moment. I beg a face-to-face farewell—then I shall die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」冀以見帝，為司宮者所遏，竟不得聞。

translations.literal: He hoped thereby to see the emperor, but was blocked by the palace attendants and in the end could not be heard.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped thereby to see the emperor, but palace attendants blocked him and in the end he could not be heard.

sentences.zh: 俄而難作，為賊所害，時年十六。

translations.literal: Before long the catastrophe broke out; he was killed by the rebels. He was sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the catastrophe broke out and he was killed by the rebels. He was sixteen.

sentences.zh: 越王越王侗字仁謹，美姿儀，性寬厚。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong, styled Renjin, was handsome in bearing and generous in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Tong, styled Renjin, was handsome in bearing and generous in nature.

sentences.zh: ，立為越王。

translations.literal: He was installed as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was installed as Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 帝每巡幸，侗常留守東都。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Tong usually remained to hold the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Tong usually remained to hold the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感作亂之際，與民部尚書樊子蓋拒之。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, he with Minister of the People Fan Zigai resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, he resisted alongside Minister of the People Fan Zigai.

sentences.zh: 及玄感平，朝于高陽，拜高陽太守。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was pacified, he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Governor of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuangan was pacified, he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Governor of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官複留守東都。

translations.literal: Before long, in his original office he again remained to hold the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again remained to hold the Eastern Capital in his original capacity.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝幸江都，複令侗與金紫光祿大夫段達、太府卿元文都、攝民部尚書韋津、右武衛將軍皇甫無逸等總留台事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again ordered Tong together with Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Duan Da, Grand Steward Yuan Wendu, Acting Minister of the People Wei Jin, General of the Right Martial Guards Huangfu Wuyi, and others jointly to oversee the affairs of the capital left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again ordered Tong, together with Duan Da, Yuan Wendu, Wei Jin, Huangfu Wuyi, and others, jointly to oversee the affairs of the capital left behind.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，文都等議，以侗元德太子之子，屬最為近，於是乃共尊立，大赦，改元曰皇泰。

translations.literal: At Yu Wen Huaji's regicide, Wendu and others deliberated that, as Tong was son of the Yuande Crown Prince, his kinship was closest; they therefore jointly raised him, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.
translations.idiomatic: At Yu Wen Huaji's regicide, Wendu and others deliberated that Tong, as son of the Yuande Crown Prince, was closest in the line of succession. They therefore jointly raised him, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.

sentences.zh: 諡帝曰明，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: The deceased emperor was given the posthumous title Ming and the temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: The deceased emperor was given the posthumous title Ming and the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 追尊元德太子為孝成皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: The Yuande Crown Prince was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaocheng with the temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuande Crown Prince was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaocheng with the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 尊其母劉良娣為皇太后。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Liu of Excellence was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Liu of Excellence, was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 以段達為納言、右翊衛大將軍、攝禮部尚書，王世充亦納言、左翊衛大將軍、攝吏部尚書，元文都內史令、左驍衛大將軍，盧楚亦內史令，皇甫無逸兵部尚書、右武衛大將軍，郭文懿內史侍郎，趙長文黃門侍郎，委以機務，為金書鐵券，藏之宮掖。

translations.literal: Duan Da was made Chief Minister, Grand General of the Right Guards, and Acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong also Chief Minister, Grand General of the Left Guards, and Acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Secretariat and Grand General of the Left Martial Guards; Lu Chu also Director of the Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and Grand General of the Right Martial Guards; Guo Wenyi Secretariat Vice Minister; Zhao Changwen Vice Minister of the Gate—entrusted with state affairs, granted golden books on iron bonds, and stored in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da was made Chief Minister, Grand General of the Right Guards, and Acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong likewise Chief Minister, Grand General of the Left Guards, and Acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Secretariat and Grand General of the Left Martial Guards; Lu Chu also Director of the Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and Grand General of the Right Martial Guards; Guo Wenyi Secretariat Vice Minister; and Zhao Changwen Vice Minister of the Gate. They were entrusted with state affairs, granted golden books on iron bonds, and stored in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 于時洛陽稱段達等為「七貴」。

translations.literal: At that time Luoyang called Duan Da and the others the "Seven Nobles."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Luoyang called Duan Da and the others the "Seven Nobles."

sentences.zh: 未幾，宇文化及立秦王子浩為天子，來次彭城，所經城邑多從逆黨。

translations.literal: Before long Yu Wen Huaji installed Prince Hao of Qin as Son of Heaven and halted at Pengcheng; the cities he passed through mostly followed the rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu Wen Huaji installed Prince Hao of Qin as Son of Heaven and halted at Pengcheng; most cities he passed through followed the rebel faction.

sentences.zh: 侗懼，遣使者蓋琮、馬公政招懷李密。

translations.literal: Tong was afraid and sent envoys Gai Cong and Ma Gongzheng to win over Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was afraid and sent envoys Gai Cong and Ma Gongzheng to win over Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密遂遣使請降，侗大悅，禮其使甚厚。

translations.literal: Li Mi thereupon sent envoys requesting surrender; Tong was greatly pleased and treated his envoys very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi thereupon sent envoys requesting surrender. Tong was greatly pleased and treated the envoys very generously.

sentences.zh: 即拜密為太尉、尚書令、魏國公，令拒化及。

translations.literal: He at once appointed Li Mi Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Wei, and ordered him to resist Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: He at once appointed Li Mi Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Wei, and ordered him to resist Huaji.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：

translations.literal: An edict was issued, which reads:
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued, which reads:

sentences.zh: :我大隋之有天下，於茲三十八載。

translations.literal: Our Great Sui's possession of the realm has now reached thirty-eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Sui's possession of the realm has now reached thirty-eight years.

sentences.zh: 高祖文皇帝聖略神功，載造區夏。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor Wen, with sacred strategy and divine merit, anew created the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Founding Emperor Wen, with sacred strategy and divine merit, anew created the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 世祖明皇帝則天法地，混一華戎。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor Ming modeled himself on heaven and earth and united Chinese and barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu Emperor Ming modeled himself on heaven and earth and united Chinese and barbarian.

sentences.zh: 東暨蟠木，西通細柳，前逾丹徼，後越幽都。

translations.literal: East to Panmu, west connecting to Xiliu, forward beyond the red frontier, rear passing Youdu.
translations.idiomatic: East to Panmu, west to Xiliu, forward beyond the red frontier, rear past Youdu.

sentences.zh: 日月之所臨，風雨之所至，圓首方足，稟氣食芼，莫不盡入提封，皆為臣妾。

translations.literal: Where sun and moon shine and wind and rain reach, every round-headed, square-footed creature that draws breath and eats vegetation—all entered the imperial domain and became subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Where sun and moon shine and wind and rain reach, every human creature that draws breath and eats vegetation—all entered the imperial domain and became subjects.

sentences.zh: 加以寶貺畢集，靈瑞咸臻，作樂制禮，移風易俗。

translations.literal: Moreover treasures gathered in full and numinous omens all arrived; music was made and rites established, customs moved and habits changed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover treasures gathered in full and numinous omens all arrived; music was made, rites established, customs moved, and habits changed.

sentences.zh: 智周寰海，萬物鹹受其賜，道濟天下，百姓用而不知。

translations.literal: Wisdom encompassed the seas; the ten thousand things all received his bounty; the Way aided the world and the common people used it without knowing.
translations.idiomatic: His wisdom encompassed the seas; the ten thousand things all received his bounty; the Way aided the world while the common people used it without knowing.

sentences.zh: 世祖往因曆試，統臨南服，自居皇極，順茲望幸。

translations.literal: Shizu formerly because of repeated trials oversaw the southern domains; since occupying the imperial pinnacle he has followed this and awaited imperial visits.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu formerly, through repeated trials, oversaw the southern domains; since occupying the imperial throne he has followed this course and awaited imperial visits.

sentences.zh: 所以往歲省方，展禮肆覲，停鑾駐蹕，按駕清道，八屯如昔，七萃不移。

translations.literal: Therefore last year he inspected the regions, displayed rites and held court audiences, halted the imperial carriage and stayed his progress, cleared the road for the procession—the eight encampments as of old, the seven hosts unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore last year he inspected the regions, displayed rites and held court audiences, halted the imperial carriage and stayed his progress, and cleared the road for the procession—the eight encampments as of old, the seven hosts unmoved.

sentences.zh: 豈意釁起非常，逮於軒陛，災生不意，延及冕旒。

translations.literal: Who could have thought misfortune would arise beyond the norm and reach the imperial hall; disaster would come unlooked-for and extend to the imperial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have thought misfortune would arise beyond the norm and reach the imperial hall, or that disaster would come unlooked-for and extend to the imperial crown?

sentences.zh: 奉諱之日，五情崩隕，攀號荼毒，不能自勝。

translations.literal: On the day of receiving the tabooed news, the five emotions collapsed; climbing and crying in bitter grief, I could not overcome myself.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of receiving the tabooed news my five emotions collapsed; climbing and crying in bitter grief, I could not overcome myself.

sentences.zh: :且聞之，自古代有屯剝，賊臣逆子，無世無之。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that from antiquity there have been times of hardship and decline; rebel ministers and unfilial sons exist in no age without them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have heard that from antiquity there have been times of hardship and decline; rebel ministers and unfilial sons exist in no age without them.

sentences.zh: 至如宇文化及，世傳庸品。

translations.literal: As for Yu Wen Huaji, his family for generations has been mediocre stock.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yu Wen Huaji, his family for generations has been mediocre stock.

sentences.zh: 其父述，往屬時來，早沾厚遇，賜以婚媾，置之公輔，位尊九命，祿重萬鐘，禮極人臣，榮冠世表。

translations.literal: His father Shu, when the times came his way, early received thick favor—granted marriage alliance, placed among chief ministers, rank honoring the nine orders, salary weighing ten thousand zhong, rites reaching the utmost for a subject, glory crowning the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu, when fortune came his way, early received thick favor—granted marriage alliance, placed among chief ministers, rank of the nine orders, salary of ten thousand zhong, rites reaching the utmost for a subject, glory crowning the age.

sentences.zh: 徒承海嶽之恩，未有涓塵之益。

translations.literal: He merely received favor vast as seas and mountains yet offered no benefit the size of a drop of dust.
translations.idiomatic: He merely received favor vast as seas and mountains yet offered no benefit the size of a drop of dust.

sentences.zh: 化及以此下材，夙蒙顧盼，出入外內，奉望階墀。

translations.literal: Huaji with this base talent early received imperial regard, going in and out within and without, attending upon the steps of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji, with this base talent, early received imperial regard, going in and out within and without and attending upon the steps of the throne.

sentences.zh: 昔陪籓國，統領禁衛，及從升皇祚，陪列九卿。

translations.literal: Formerly he accompanied the princely state, commanding the forbidden guard; when he followed ascent to the imperial throne he ranked among the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly he accompanied the princely establishment, commanding the forbidden guard; when he followed ascent to the imperial throne he ranked among the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 但本性兇狠，恣其貪穢，或交結惡黨，或侵掠貨財，事重刑篇，狀盈獄簡。

translations.literal: But his nature was fierce and cruel; he indulged greed and corruption, either joining wicked factions or plundering goods and wealth—matters weighty in the penal code, cases filling the prison records.
translations.idiomatic: But his nature was fierce and cruel. He indulged greed and corruption, joining wicked factions or plundering goods and wealth—matters weighty in the penal code, cases filling the prison records.

sentences.zh: 在上不遺簪履，恩加草芥，應至死辜，每蒙恕免。

translations.literal: The sovereign above did not cast away even sandals and shoes; grace was added like grass and husks—though deserving death for capital guilt, each time he received pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign did not cast away even sandals and shoes; grace was added like grass and husks—though deserving death for capital guilt, each time he received pardon.

sentences.zh: 三經除解，尋複本職，再徙邊裔，仍即追還。

translations.literal: Three times dismissed from office, soon restored to his original post; twice transferred to border regions, yet immediately recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Three times dismissed from office, soon restored to his original post; twice transferred to border regions, yet immediately recalled.

sentences.zh: 生成之恩，昊天罔極，獎擢之義，人事罕聞。

translations.literal: The grace of giving life—vast as heaven without limit; the meaning of promotion and elevation—rarely heard among men.
translations.idiomatic: The grace of giving life was vast as heaven without limit; the meaning of promotion and elevation was rarely heard among men.

sentences.zh: 化及梟獍為心，禽獸不若，縱毒興禍，傾覆行宮。

translations.literal: Huaji had the heart of an owl and a porcupine, worse than beasts; he unleashed poison and raised calamity, overturning the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji had the heart of an owl and a porcupine, worse than beasts. He unleashed poison and raised calamity, overturning the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 諸王兄弟，一時殘酷，痛暴行路，世不忍言。

translations.literal: The princely brothers at one time were cruelly slaughtered; the pain on the roads was unbearable—the age could not bear to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The princely brothers were at one time cruelly slaughtered; the pain on the roads was unbearable—the age could not bear to speak of it.

sentences.zh: 有窮之在夏時，犬戎之于周代，釁辱之極，亦未是過。

translations.literal: Youqiong in the Xia age, the Quanrong in the Zhou age—the utmost of insult and shame was not surpassed.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiong in the Xia age, the Quanrong in the Zhou age—even their utmost of insult and shame was not surpassed.

sentences.zh: 朕所以刻骨崩心，飲膽嘗血，瞻天視地，無處容身。

translations.literal: I therefore gnaw bone and shatter heart, drink gall and taste blood, look to heaven and view earth—nowhere to contain my person.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore gnaw bone and shatter heart, drink gall and taste blood, look to heaven and view earth—nowhere to contain myself.

sentences.zh: :今王公卿士，庶僚百辟，鹹以大寶鴻名，不可顛墜，元兇巨猾，須早夷殄，翼戴朕躬，嗣守寶位。

translations.literal: Now the kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars, the hundred officials of all ranks—all deem the great treasure and august name cannot be overturned; the arch-criminal and great villain must early be exterminated; support and bear up my person to succeed and guard the precious throne.
translations.idiomatic: Now kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars, the hundred officials of all ranks—all deem the great treasure and august name cannot be overturned; the arch-criminal and great villain must early be exterminated; they support and bear up my person to succeed and guard the precious throne.

sentences.zh: 顧惟寡薄，志不逮此。

translations.literal: Looking to my paltry thinness, my will does not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: Looking to my paltry thinness, my will does not reach this.

sentences.zh: 今者出黼扆而杖旄鉞，釋衰麻而擐甲胄，銜冤誓眾，忍淚治兵，指日遄征，以平大盜。

translations.literal: Now I go forth from the embroidered screen bearing battle-axes, cast off mourning hemp and don armor, harboring grievance to swear the host, holding back tears to order troops—on the appointed day swiftly to campaign and pacify the great robber.
translations.idiomatic: Now I go forth from the embroidered screen bearing battle-axes, cast off mourning hemp and don armor, harboring grievance to swear the host and holding back tears to order troops—on the appointed day swiftly to campaign and pacify the great robber.

sentences.zh: 且化及偽立秦王之子，幽遏比於囚拘，其身自稱霸相，專擅擬於九五。

translations.literal: Moreover Huaji falsely installed the son of the Prince of Qin, confining and restraining him as if in prison; he himself called himself hegemon and minister, usurping and monopolizing the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Huaji falsely installed the son of the Prince of Qin, confining him as if in prison; he himself styled himself hegemon and minister, usurping the imperial position.

sentences.zh: 履踐禁禦，據有宮闈，昂首揚眉，初無慚色。

translations.literal: He trod the forbidden precincts and occupied the palace inner quarters, raising head and arching brows, at first without shame.
translations.idiomatic: He trod the forbidden precincts and occupied the palace inner quarters, raising his head and arching his brows without shame.

sentences.zh: 衣冠朝望，外懼凶威，志士誠臣，內皆憤怨。

translations.literal: The courtly gentry outwardly feared his fierce might; loyal scholars inwardly all harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: The courtly gentry outwardly feared his fierce might; loyal scholars inwardly all harbored anger.

sentences.zh: 以我義師，順彼天道，梟夷醜族，匪夕伊朝。

translations.literal: With our righteous army following their heaven-violating way, the owl and villain clan will be exterminated—not one morning and evening away.
translations.idiomatic: With our righteous army following heaven's way against their rebellion, the villain clan will be exterminated—not one morning and evening away.

sentences.zh: :太尉、尚書令、魏公丹誠內發，宏略外舉，率勤王之師，討違天之逆。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Wei—red sincerity issuing within, grand strategy raised without—leads the army loyal to the throne to punish heaven-defying rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Wei—red sincerity issuing within, grand strategy raised without—leads the army loyal to the throne to punish heaven-defying rebellion.

sentences.zh: 果毅爭先，熊羆競逐，金鼓振讋，若火焚毛，鋒刃縱橫，如湯沃雪。

translations.literal: The resolute vied to be first; bears and panthers raced in pursuit; gold drums shook terror like fire burning fur; blades crossed like boiling water pouring on snow.
translations.idiomatic: The resolute vied to be first; bears and panthers raced in pursuit. Gold drums shook terror like fire burning fur; blades crossed like boiling water pouring on snow.

sentences.zh: 魏公志在匡濟，投袂前驅，朕親禦六軍，星言繼進。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei's will is to aid the realm; he flings his sleeves and drives forward; I personally lead the six armies and at star-speed follow in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei's will is to aid the realm; he flings his sleeves and drives forward. I personally lead the six armies and at star-speed follow in advance.

sentences.zh: 以此眾戰，以斯順舉，擘山可以動，射石可以入。

translations.literal: With this host to battle, with this accord to raise—splitting mountains can be moved, shooting stone can penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: With this host to battle and this accord to raise—splitting mountains can be moved and shooting stone can penetrate.

sentences.zh: 況擁此人徒，皆有離德，京都侍衛，西憶鄉家，江左淳民，南思邦邑，比來表書駱驛，人信相尋。

translations.literal: How much more those who hold this rabble—all have divided hearts; the capital guards long for home in the west, the pure folk of the Jiang left southward yearn for their districts; recently memorials and letters have come in strings, men and trust following one another.
translations.idiomatic: How much more those who hold this rabble—all have divided hearts. The capital guards long for home in the west; the pure folk of the Jiang left southward yearn for their districts. Recently memorials and letters have come in strings, trust following one upon another.

sentences.zh: 若王師一臨，舊章暫睹，自應解甲倒戈，冰銷葉散。

translations.literal: If the royal army arrives once, and they briefly see the old standards, they should of themselves lay down armor and turn their spears—ice melting and leaves scattering.
translations.idiomatic: If the royal army arrives once and they briefly see the old standards, they should of themselves lay down armor and turn their spears—like ice melting and leaves scattering.

sentences.zh: 且聞化及自恣，天奪其心，殺戮不辜，挫辱人士，莫不道路仄目，號天踞地。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear Huaji indulges himself; heaven has taken his heart; he slaughters the innocent and humiliates gentlemen—all on the roads narrow their eyes, crying to heaven and stamping the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I hear Huaji indulges himself and heaven has taken his heart. He slaughters the innocent and humiliates gentlemen—all on the roads narrow their eyes, crying to heaven and stamping the earth.

sentences.zh: 朕今復仇雪恥，梟轘者一人，拯溺救焚，所哀者士庶。

translations.literal: I now take revenge and wash shame; the one to be beheaded and minced is one man; saving the drowning and rescuing the burning—what I pity is scholars and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: I now take revenge and wash shame. The one to be beheaded is one man; saving the drowning and rescuing the burning—what I pity is scholars and commoners.

sentences.zh: 唯天鑒孔殷，祐我宗社，億兆感義，俱會朕心。

translations.literal: May heaven alone look down in deep compassion, protect our altars of soil and grain; the hundred millions moved by righteousness all meet my heart.
translations.idiomatic: May heaven alone look down in deep compassion and protect our altars of soil and grain; the hundred millions, moved by righteousness, all meet my heart.

sentences.zh: 梟戮元兇，策勳飲至，四海交泰，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Behead and slaughter the arch-criminal; record merit and drink to the utmost; within the four seas all is at peace—this is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Behead the arch-criminal; record merit and drink to the utmost; within the four seas all is at peace—this is my wish.

sentences.zh: 兵術軍機，並受魏公節度。

translations.literal: Military arts and army strategy—all receive the Duke of Wei's command.
translations.idiomatic: Military arts and army strategy all receive the Duke of Wei's command.

sentences.zh: 密見使者，大悅，北面拜伏，臣禮甚恭。

translations.literal: When Li Mi saw the envoys he was greatly pleased, bowed facing north in prostration, and his ministerly courtesy was very respectful.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi saw the envoys he was greatly pleased, bowed facing north in prostration, and his ministerly courtesy was very respectful.

sentences.zh: 密遂東拒化及。

translations.literal: Li Mi thereupon resisted Huaji to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi thereupon resisted Huaji to the east.

sentences.zh: 「七貴」頗不協，陰有相圖之計。

translations.literal: The "Seven Nobles" were quite discordant and secretly had designs of plotting against one another.
translations.idiomatic: The "Seven Nobles" were quite discordant and secretly plotted against one another.

sentences.zh: 未幾，元文都、盧楚、郭文懿、趙長文等為世充所殺，皇甫無逸遁歸長安。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Shichong; Huangfu Wuyi fled and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Shichong; Huangfu Wuyi fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 世充詣侗所陳謝，辭情哀苦。

translations.literal: Shichong went to Tong's place to offer apology; his words were bitterly sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong went to Tong's place to offer apology; his words were bitterly sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 侗以為至誠，命之上殿，被發為盟，誓無貳志。

translations.literal: Tong regarded him as utterly sincere, ordered him up to the hall, let down his hair to swear alliance, vowing no second intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tong regarded him as utterly sincere, ordered him up to the hall, let down his hair to swear alliance, and vowed no second intent.

sentences.zh: 自是侗無所關預。

translations.literal: From this Tong had nothing to decide.
translations.idiomatic: From this Tong had nothing to decide.

sentences.zh: 侗心不能平，遂與記室陸士季謀圖世充，事不果而止。

translations.literal: Tong's heart could not be at peace; he therefore with Recorder Lu Shiji plotted against Shichong, but the matter did not succeed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's heart could not be at peace. He plotted with Recorder Lu Shiji against Shichong, but the matter did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 及世充破李密，眾望益歸之，遂自為鄭王，總百揆，加九錫，備法物，侗不能禁也。

translations.literal: When Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular expectation increasingly turned to him; he thereupon made himself Prince of Zheng, oversaw all government affairs, was granted the nine bestowals, and prepared the ritual regalia—Tong could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular expectation increasingly turned to him. He made himself Prince of Zheng, oversaw all government affairs, was granted the nine bestowals, and prepared the ritual regalia—Tong could not forbid it.

sentences.zh: 段達、雲定興等十人入見於侗曰：「天命不常，鄭王功德甚盛，願陛下揖讓告禪，遵唐、虞之跡。

translations.literal: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others entered to see Tong, saying: "Heaven's mandate is not constant; the Prince of Zheng's merit and virtue are very abundant. We wish Your Majesty to yield and announce abdication, following the traces of Tang and Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others entered to see Tong, saying, "Heaven's mandate is not constant; the Prince of Zheng's merit and virtue are very abundant. We wish Your Majesty to yield and announce abdication, following the traces of Tang and Yu."

sentences.zh: 」侗聞之怒曰：「天下者，高祖之天下，東都者，世祖之東都。

translations.literal: Tong heard this and angrily said: "The realm is the realm of the Founding Emperor; the Eastern Capital is the Eastern Capital of Shizu."
translations.idiomatic: Tong heard this and said angrily, "The realm is the Founding Emperor's realm; the Eastern Capital is Shizu's Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 若隋德未衰，此言不可發；

translations.literal: If Sui virtue has not yet declined, this speech must not be uttered;
translations.idiomatic: If Sui virtue has not yet declined, this speech must not be uttered;

sentences.zh: 必天命有改，亦何論於禪讓！

translations.literal: if Heaven's mandate truly must change, what need to speak of abdication!
translations.idiomatic: if Heaven's mandate truly must change, what need to speak of abdication!

sentences.zh: 公等或先朝舊臣，績宣上代，或勤王立節，身服軒冕，忽有斯言，朕複當何所望！

translations.literal: You are either old ministers of the former court who performed merit for the previous generation, or men who established merit in aiding the throne and personally wore court caps—suddenly to have this speech, what may I again look to!
translations.idiomatic: You are either old ministers of the former court who performed merit for the previous generation, or men who established merit in aiding the throne and personally wore court caps—suddenly to have this speech, what may I again look to!

sentences.zh: 」神色懍然，侍衛者莫不流汗。

translations.literal: His expression was stern; the attendants all sweated.
translations.idiomatic: His expression was stern; the attendants all sweated.

sentences.zh: 既而退朝，對良娣而泣。

translations.literal: He then withdrew from court and wept facing the Lady of Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew from court and wept before the Lady of Excellence.

sentences.zh: 世充更使人謂侗曰：「今海內未定，須得長君。

translations.literal: Shichong again sent someone to say to Tong: "Now within the seas is not yet settled; a long-reigning ruler is needed."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong again sent someone to say to Tong, "Now the realm is not yet settled; a long-reigning ruler is needed."

sentences.zh: 待四方乂安，複子明辟，必若前盟，義不違負。

translations.literal: When the four quarters are at peace, I shall restore you to the bright throne; if it is like the former oath, righteousness will not violate the burden.
translations.idiomatic: When the four quarters are at peace I shall restore you to the bright throne; if it is like the former oath, I shall not violate my word.

sentences.zh: 」侗不得已，遜位於世充，遂被幽於含涼殿。

translations.literal: Tong had no alternative; he yielded the throne to Shichong and was thereupon confined in the Hanliang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had no alternative. He yielded the throne to Shichong and was thereupon confined in the Hanliang Hall.

sentences.zh: 世充僭偽號，封為潞國公，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: Shichong usurped a false title and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong usurped a false title and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 月餘，宇文儒童、裴仁基等謀誅世充，複尊立侗，事泄，並見害。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Shichong and again raise Tong; the matter was exposed and they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Shichong and again raise Tong. The matter was exposed and they were all killed.

sentences.zh: 世充兄世惲因勸世充害侗，以絕民望。

translations.literal: Shichong's elder brother Shiyun thereupon urged Shichong to kill Tong to cut off popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's elder brother Shiyun urged Shichong to kill Tong to cut off popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 世充遣其侄行本齎鴆詣侗所曰：「願皇帝飲此酒。

translations.literal: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben bearing poisoned wine to Tong's place, saying: "I wish the emperor to drink this wine."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben bearing poisoned wine to Tong's place, saying, "I wish the emperor to drink this wine."

sentences.zh: 」侗知不免，請與母相見，不許。

translations.literal: Tong knew he could not escape and requested to see his mother; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tong knew he could not escape and requested to see his mother; it was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 遂布席焚香禮佛，咒曰：「從今以去，願不生帝王尊貴之家。

translations.literal: He thereupon spread mats, burned incense, and worshiped the Buddha, cursing: "From now onward, may I not be born into a family of imperial honor and nobility."
translations.idiomatic: He spread mats, burned incense, and worshiped the Buddha, cursing, "From now onward may I not be born into a family of imperial honor and nobility."

sentences.zh: 」於是仰藥。

translations.literal: He then raised the drug to his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He then drank the poison.

sentences.zh: 不能時絕，更以帛縊之。

translations.literal: He could not die at once; they again strangled him with silk.
translations.idiomatic: He could not die at once; they strangled him again with silk.

sentences.zh: 世充偽諡為恭皇帝。

translations.literal: Shichong falsely gave the posthumous title Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong falsely gave the posthumous title Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 齊王齊王暕，字世朏，小字阿孩。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jian, styled Shihui, childhood name Ahai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Jian, styled Shihui, childhood name Ahai.

sentences.zh: 美容儀，疏眉目，少為高祖所愛。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing, with sparse eyebrows and eyes, in youth he was loved by the Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, with sparse eyebrows and eyes, in youth he was loved by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，立為豫章王，邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he was installed as Prince of Yuzhang with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era he was installed as Prince of Yuzhang with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗涉經史，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: When he grew up he broadly studied the classics and histories and was especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he broadly studied the classics and histories and was especially skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初為內史令。

translations.literal: At first he was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，拜揚州總管沿淮以南諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou for all military affairs south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou for all military affairs south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，進封齊王，增邑四千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne he was advanced to Prince of Qi and his fief was increased by four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne he was advanced to Prince of Qi and his fief increased by four thousand households.

sentences.zh: ，帝初入東都，盛陳鹵簿，暕為軍導。

translations.literal: When the emperor first entered the Eastern Capital he displayed a magnificent guard of honor; Jian was army guide.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first entered the Eastern Capital he displayed a magnificent guard of honor; Jian served as army guide.

sentences.zh: 尋轉豫州牧。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 俄而元德太子薨，朝野注望，鹹以暕當嗣。

translations.literal: Before long the Yuande Crown Prince died; court and countryside fixed their hopes—all deemed Jian should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Yuande Crown Prince died. Court and countryside fixed their hopes on Jian as the one who should succeed.

sentences.zh: 帝又敕吏部尚書牛弘妙選官屬，公卿由是多進子弟。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to select officials with care; dukes and ministers therefore mostly advanced their sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to select officials with care, and dukes and ministers therefore mostly advanced their sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉雍州牧，尋徙河南尹、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province; soon he was moved to Governor of Henan and made Palace Attendant of the First Order with the privilege of an independent staff.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province, and soon he was made Governor of Henan and Palace Attendant of the First Order with an independent staff.

sentences.zh: 元德太子左右二萬餘人悉隸於暕，寵遇益隆，自樂平公主及諸戚屬競來致禮，百官稱謁，填咽道路。

translations.literal: The more than twenty thousand attendants of the Yuande Crown Prince all came under Jian's command; favor and treatment grew ever more lofty. From Princess of Yueping and all the kin, they vied to come with gifts; officials paid calls until the roads were choked.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuande Crown Prince's more than twenty thousand attendants all came under Jian's command, and his favor grew ever more lofty. From Princess of Yueping and all the kinfolk they vied to bring gifts; officials paid calls until the roads were choked.

sentences.zh: 暕頗驕恣，昵近小人，所行多不法，遣喬令則、劉虔安、裴該、皇甫諶、庫狄仲錡、陳智偉等求聲色狗馬。

translations.literal: Jian was quite arrogant and willful, intimate with petty men; what he did was mostly unlawful. He sent Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, Kudiji Zhongqi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to seek sound, color, dogs, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was quite arrogant and willful and intimate with petty men; most of what he did was unlawful. He sent Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, Kudiji Zhongqi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to seek pleasures, women, dogs, and horses.

sentences.zh: 令則等因此放縱，訪人家有女者，輒矯暕命呼之，載入暕宅，因緣藏隱，恣行淫穢，而後遣之。

translations.literal: Lingze and the others therefore ran wild; wherever they found a household with a daughter they would falsely use Jian's command to summon her, load her into Jian's residence, use connections to hide her, indulge in lewdness as they pleased, and afterward send her away.
translations.idiomatic: Lingze and the others ran wild. Wherever they found a household with a daughter they falsely used Jian's command to summon her, brought her into his residence, hid her through connections, indulged in lewdness, and afterward sent her away.

sentences.zh: 仲錡、智偉二人詣隴西，撾炙諸胡，責其名馬，得數匹以進於。

translations.literal: Zhongqi and Zhiwei two men went to Longxi, roasted the various Hu, demanded their famous horses, and obtained several mounts to present to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi and Zhiwei went to Longxi, extorted the frontier Hu by roasting them, demanded their famous horses, and obtained several mounts to present to the prince.

sentences.zh: 暕令還主，仲錡等詐言王賜，將歸於家，暕不之知也。

translations.literal: Jian ordered them returned to their owners; Zhongqi and the others falsely said the prince had bestowed them and were about to take them home—Jian did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian ordered the horses returned to their owners, but Zhongqi and the others falsely said the prince had bestowed them and were taking them home—Jian did not know.

sentences.zh: 又樂平公主嘗奏帝，言柳氏女美者，帝未有所答。

translations.literal: Moreover Princess of Yueping once memorialized the emperor, saying the daughter of the Liu clan was beautiful; the emperor had not yet answered.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Yueping once memorialized the emperor that the Liu clan's daughter was beautiful; the emperor had not yet answered.

sentences.zh: 久之，主複以柳氏進於暕，暕習納之。

translations.literal: After a long time the princess again presented the Liu woman to Jian; Jian readily took her in.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time the princess again presented the Liu woman to Jian, and he readily took her in.

sentences.zh: 其後帝問主柳氏女所在，主曰：「在齊王所。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor asked the princess where the Liu daughter was; the princess said: "She is at the Prince of Qi's place."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor asked the princess where the Liu daughter was. The princess said, "She is with the Prince of Qi."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 暕于東都營第，大門無故而崩，聽事栿中折，識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: Jian built a mansion in the Eastern Capital; the great gate for no reason collapsed and the audience hall ridge-beam broke in the middle—those who knew deemed it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Jian built a mansion in the Eastern Capital. The great gate for no reason collapsed and the audience-hall ridge-beam broke in the middle—those who knew deemed it inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 其後從帝幸榆林，暕督後軍步騎五萬，恆與帝相去數十裡而舍。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed the emperor to Yulin; Jian commanded the rear army of fifty thousand foot and horse, always encamping several tens of li from the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he followed the emperor to Yulin. Jian commanded the rear army of fifty thousand foot and horse, always encamping several tens of li from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會帝于汾陽宮大獵，詔暕以千騎入圍。

translations.literal: It happened the emperor was on a great hunt at Fenyang Palace and ordered Jian to enter the enclosure with a thousand riders.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor held a great hunt at Fenyang Palace, he ordered Jian to enter the enclosure with a thousand riders.

sentences.zh: 暕大獲麋鹿以獻，而帝未有得也，乃怒從官，皆言為暕左右所遏，獸不得前。

translations.literal: Jian took many elk and deer to present, but the emperor had not yet obtained any; he thereupon grew angry at the attendants, all saying Jian's men had blocked them and the beasts could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jian took many elk and deer to present, but the emperor had obtained none and grew angry at his attendants, who all said Jian's men had blocked the beasts so they could not advance.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發怒，求暕罪失。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry and sought Jian's faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon grew angry and sought Jian's faults.

sentences.zh: 時制縣令無故不得出境，有伊闕令皇甫詡幸於暕，違禁將之汾陽宮。

translations.literal: At that time the regulation was that magistrates could not leave their districts without cause; the magistrate of Yique Huangfu Xu, favored by Jian, violated the prohibition and took him to Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time magistrates could not leave their districts without cause, but Huangfu Xu, magistrate of Yique and favored by Jian, violated the prohibition and took him to Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 又京兆人達奚通有妾王氏善歌，貴遊宴聚，多或要致，於是輾轉亦出入王家。

translations.literal: Moreover Daxi Tong of Jingzhao had a concubine Lady Wang skilled in song; at noble outings and banquets many would request her—thus by turns she also went in and out of the Wang household.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Daxi Tong of Jingzhao had a concubine, Lady Wang, skilled in song. At noble outings and banquets many would request her, and thus by turns she also went in and out of the Wang household.

sentences.zh: 禦史韋德裕希旨劾暕，帝令甲士千餘大索暕第，因窮治其事。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Deyu to please the emperor impeached Jian; the emperor ordered more than a thousand armored soldiers to search Jian's residence thoroughly and pursue the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Deyu, to please the emperor, impeached Jian. The emperor ordered more than a thousand armored soldiers to search Jian's residence thoroughly and pursue the matter to the end.

sentences.zh: 暕妃韋氏者，民部尚書沖之女也，早卒，暕遂與妃姊元氏婦通，遂產一女，外人皆不得知。

translations.literal: Jian's consort was of the Wei clan, daughter of Minister of the People Chong; she died early. Jian then had relations with the consort's elder sister, wife of the Yuan clan, and she bore a daughter—outsiders all did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's consort was of the Wei clan, daughter of Minister of the People Chong; she died early. Jian then had relations with the consort's elder sister, wife of the Yuan clan, and she bore a daughter unknown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 陰引喬令則於第內酣宴，令則稱慶，脫暕帽以為歡樂。

translations.literal: He secretly brought in Qiao Lingze for a hearty banquet within the residence; Lingze offered congratulations and removed Jian's cap for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly brought Qiao Lingze in for a hearty banquet at the residence. Lingze offered congratulations and removed Jian's cap for amusement.

sentences.zh: 召相工令遍視後庭，相工指妃姊曰：「此產子者當為皇后。

translations.literal: He summoned a physiognomist to survey the rear courtyard throughout; the physiognomist pointed to the consort's elder sister and said: "This one who bears a child will become empress."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned a physiognomist to survey the entire rear courtyard. The physiognomist pointed to the consort's elder sister and said, "The woman who bears a child here will become empress."

sentences.zh: 王貴不可言。

translations.literal: The prince's nobility is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's nobility is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」時國無儲副，暕自謂次當得立。

translations.literal: At that time the state had no heir apparent; Jian himself deemed that as second son he ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the state had no heir apparent; Jian deemed that as second son he ought to be established.

sentences.zh: 又以元德太子有三子，內常不安，陰挾左道，為厭勝之事。

translations.literal: Moreover because the Yuande Crown Prince had three sons, inwardly he was constantly uneasy and secretly relied on heterodox ways, performing sorcery for subjugation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because the Yuande Crown Prince had three sons, he was inwardly uneasy and secretly relied on heterodox arts, performing sorcery for subjugation.

sentences.zh: 至是，事皆發，帝大怒，斬令則等數人，妃姊賜死，暕府僚皆斥之邊遠。

translations.literal: At this time all the matters came out; the emperor was greatly angry, beheaded Lingze and several others, the consort's elder sister was ordered to die, and Jian's staff were all banished to distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: At this time all the matters came out. The emperor was greatly angry, beheaded Lingze and several others, ordered the consort's elder sister to die, and banished all of Jian's staff to distant regions.

sentences.zh: 時趙王杲猶在孩孺，帝謂侍臣曰：「朕唯有暕一子，不然者，當肆諸市朝，以明國憲也。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Zhao Gao was still an infant; the emperor said to attendants: "I have only Jian as one son—otherwise I would expose him in the marketplace to clarify the state's law."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Zhao Gao was still an infant. The emperor said to his attendants, "I have only Jian as one son—otherwise I would expose him in the marketplace to clarify the state's law."

sentences.zh: 」暕自是恩寵日衰，雖為京尹，不復關預時政。

translations.literal: From this Jian's favor daily declined; though he was Governor of the Capital, he no longer participated in current government.
translations.idiomatic: From this Jian's favor daily declined. Though he was Governor of the Capital, he no longer participated in government.

sentences.zh: 帝恆令武賁郎將一人監其府事，暕有微失，武賁輒奏之。

translations.literal: The emperor always ordered one Tiger Guard officer to supervise his residence affairs; if Jian had a slight fault the Tiger Guard at once reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always ordered one Tiger Guard officer to supervise his residence. If Jian had the slightest fault the officer at once reported it.

sentences.zh: 帝亦常慮暕生變，所給左右，皆以老弱，備員而已。

translations.literal: The emperor also constantly feared Jian would raise a coup; those given him as attendants were all old and weak—names on the roster only.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also constantly feared Jian would raise a coup. Those given him as attendants were all old and weak—names on the roster only.

sentences.zh: 暕每懷危懼，心不自安。

translations.literal: Jian constantly harbored dread and his heart was not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jian constantly harbored dread and could not be at peace in his heart.

sentences.zh: 又帝在江都宮，元會，暕具法服將朝，無故有血從裳中而下。

translations.literal: Moreover when the emperor was at the Jiangdu palace for the New Year audience, Jian put on full court dress to attend court; for no reason blood flowed down from within his robe.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at the Jiangdu palace for the New Year audience, Jian put on full court dress to attend. For no reason blood flowed down from within his robe.

sentences.zh: 又坐齋中，見群鼠數十，至前而死，視皆無頭。

translations.literal: Again while sitting in his study he saw several tens of rats come before him and die; looking closely, all were headless.
translations.idiomatic: Again while sitting in his study he saw several tens of rats come before him and die; all were headless.

sentences.zh: 暕意甚惡之。

translations.literal: Jian's mind was very averse to this.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was deeply disturbed by this.

sentences.zh: 俄而化及作亂，兵將犯蹕，帝聞，顧謂蕭後曰：「得非阿孩邪？

translations.literal: Before long Huaji raised rebellion and troops were about to violate the imperial progress; the emperor heard and, turning to Empress Xiao, said: "Could it not be Ahai?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huaji raised rebellion and troops were about to violate the imperial progress. The emperor heard and, turning to Empress Xiao, said, "Could it not be Ahai?"

sentences.zh: 」其見疏忌如此。

translations.literal: Such was the estrangement and suspicion he suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the estrangement and suspicion he suffered.

sentences.zh: 化及複令人捕暕，暕時尚臥未起，賊既進，暕驚曰：「是何人？

translations.literal: Huaji again sent men to seize Jian; Jian was still in bed and had not risen; when the rebels entered, Jian startled and said: "What persons are these?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji again sent men to seize Jian. Jian was still in bed and had not risen. When the rebels entered he startled and said, "What persons are these?"

sentences.zh: 」莫有報者，暕猶謂帝令捕之，因曰：「詔使且緩。

translations.literal: No one answered; Jian still thought the emperor had ordered his arrest and therefore said: "The edict-envoy may wait a moment."
translations.idiomatic: No one answered. Jian still thought the emperor had ordered his arrest and said, "The edict-envoy may wait a moment."

sentences.zh: 兒不負國家。

translations.literal: Your son has not failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: Your son has not failed the state.

sentences.zh: 」賊於是曳至街而斬之，及其二子亦遇害。

translations.literal: The rebels thereupon dragged him to the street and beheaded him; his two sons also met harm.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dragged him to the street and beheaded him, and his two sons also met harm.

sentences.zh: 暕竟不知殺者為誰。

translations.literal: Jian to the end did not know who his killers were.
translations.idiomatic: Jian never knew who his killers were.

sentences.zh: 時年三十四。

translations.literal: He was thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 有遺腹子政道，與蕭後同入突厥，處羅可汗號為隋王，中國人沒入北蕃者，悉配之以為部落，以定襄城處之。

translations.literal: He had a posthumous son Zhengdao who with Empress Xiao entered the Turks together; Khan Chuluo styled him Prince of Sui; Chinese taken captive in the northern frontier were all assigned to him as tribes and settled at Dingxiang city.
translations.idiomatic: He had a posthumous son, Zhengdao, who entered the Turks together with Empress Xiao. Khan Chuluo styled him Prince of Sui, and Chinese taken captive in the northern frontier were all assigned to him as tribes and settled at Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 及突厥滅，歸於大唐，授員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Turks were destroyed he returned to Great Tang and was appointed Vice Gentleman for Attendant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks were destroyed he returned to the Tang and was appointed Vice Gentleman for Attendant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 趙王趙王杲，小字季子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Gao, childhood name Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Gao, childhood name Jizi.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，以封趙王。

translations.literal: At seven years he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 尋授光祿大夫，拜河南尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 從幸淮南，詔行江都太守事。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Huainan, he was ordered to act as Governor of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor to Huainan, he was ordered to act as Governor of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 杲聰令，美容儀，帝有所制詞賦，杲多能誦之。

translations.literal: Gao was clever and bright, handsome in bearing; compositions and rhapsodies the emperor made—Gao mostly could recite them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was clever and bright and handsome in bearing. Compositions and rhapsodies the emperor made—Gao could mostly recite them.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，常見帝風動不進膳，杲亦終日不食。

translations.literal: His nature was utmost filial; whenever he saw the emperor troubled by wind and unable to eat, Gao also would not eat all day.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was utmost filial. Whenever he saw the emperor troubled by wind and unable to eat, Gao also would not eat all day.

sentences.zh: 又蕭後當灸，杲先請試炷，後不許之，杲泣請曰：「後所服藥，皆蒙嘗之。

translations.literal: Moreover when Empress Xiao was to undergo moxibustion, Gao first requested to test the moxa cone; the empress did not permit it. Gao wept and begged, saying: "Medicines the empress takes—I have all tasted them."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiao was to undergo moxibustion, Gao first asked to test the moxa cone. The empress did not permit it. Gao wept and begged, "Medicines the empress takes—I have tasted them all."

sentences.zh: 今灸，願聽嘗炷。

translations.literal: Now for moxibustion, I wish to be allowed to taste the cone.
translations.idiomatic: Now for moxibustion, I wish to be allowed to taste the cone.

sentences.zh: 」悲咽不已。

translations.literal: He sobbed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed without cease.

sentences.zh: 後竟為其停灸，由是尤愛之。

translations.literal: The empress in the end stopped the moxibustion for his sake; because of this he was especially loved.
translations.idiomatic: The empress in the end stopped the moxibustion for his sake, and because of this he was especially loved.

sentences.zh: 後遇化及反，杲在帝側，號慟不已。

translations.literal: Afterward when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the emperor's side and wailed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the emperor's side and wailed without cease.

sentences.zh: 裴虔通使賊斬之於帝前，血湔禦服。

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong had the rebels behead him before the emperor; blood splashed the imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong had the rebels behead him before the emperor, and blood splashed the imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 時年十二。

translations.literal: He was twelve.
translations.idiomatic: He was twelve.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：元德太子雅性謹重，有君人之量，降年不永，哀哉！

translations.literal: 【Discussion】 The historiographer says: The Yuande Crown Prince in elegant nature was careful and weighty and had the measure of a ruler; his years were not long—alas!
translations.idiomatic: 【Discussion】 The historiographer says: The Yuande Crown Prince was careful and weighty in elegant nature and had the measure of a ruler, but his years were not long—alas!

sentences.zh: 齊王敏慧可稱，志不及遠，頗懷驕僭，故煬帝疏而忌之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi was clever and could be praised, but his will did not reach far and he quite harbored arrogance and overstepping—therefore Emperor Yang estranged and suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi was clever and praiseworthy, but his will did not reach far and he harbored arrogance and overstepping—therefore Emperor Yang estranged and suspected him.

sentences.zh: 心無父子之親，貌展君臣之敬，身非積善，國有餘殃。

translations.literal: In heart he had no father-son affection; in appearance he displayed minister-ruler respect—his person did not accumulate goodness, and the state had surplus calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In heart he had no father-son affection; in appearance he displayed minister-ruler respect. His person did not accumulate goodness, and the state had surplus calamity.

sentences.zh: 至令趙及燕、越皆不得其死，悲夫！

translations.literal: To the point that Zhao and Yan and Yue all did not obtain natural deaths—lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: To the point that the princes of Zhao, Yan, and Yue all did not obtain natural deaths—lamentable!
